SBA’s finance guidance explains the accounting foundation, but the project needs its own dated facts. A balance sheet describes wealth and obligations; the funding schedule describes what can pay the actual project bills.

sections.heading: Calculate the gap without counting money twice
paragraphs: The fictional project requirement is $250,000 + $150,000 = $400,000. Allocated accessible funding is $200,000. The remaining gap is $200,000 unless additional committed capital is established. Reported net worth does not fill that gap by itself.
This result is deliberately limited to the teaching assumptions. It is not a certification of a real partner’s solvency, proof of an actual cash balance or a universal reserve requirement.

rows: Itemise costs and when they fall due

sections.heading: Work through the sources, not just the candidate’s headline
paragraphs: The finance lead creates a row for each proposed source: owner, currency, conversion assumption, restrictions, available date, approval conditions and competing uses. A source that still depends on an uncommitted loan remains unresolved. Record who is authorised to release or commit each source, not just whose name appears as owner.

If the candidate later identifies another source, the team checks whether it is genuinely additional and available when needed. Reusing the same pledged asset in two explanations would not create two sources. This reasoning exercise introduces no new fictional funding result.

sections.heading: Choose a next action that resolves the shortfall
paragraphs: Prepare descriptions and evidence status in the planning tool; handle any necessary sensitive confirmations securely outside it. No bank-statement upload or financial-document collection is required here.

Management can investigate additional capital, reduce the first-stage scope, stage rights or pause. It should also test the downside cash peak before deciding the reserve, rather than selecting a convenient percentage.
bullets: Separate reported wealth, liquid assets and allocated commitments.
Give each source a date, owner and restrictions.
List collateral, pledges and other ventures using the same money.
Keep conditional borrowing and self-reporting clearly marked.
Tie the proposed solution to the dates when the project needs cash.

practicalOutput: A dated funding bridge showing project uses, genuinely available sources, restrictions and the action needed to resolve the remaining gap.
limitations: No partner solvency certification or collection of bank statements.

title: Fictional case: earn wider territory through demonstrated service capability
description: An operator’s request for several states needs customer, staffing and account-allocation evidence.
learningSummary: A fictional Dutch industrial-maintenance brand considers a capable regional operator’s request for rights across several U.S. states. A large map can look like a growth plan while hiding long journeys, different customers and unsupported delivery promises. This exercise turns the territory request into staged commercial decisions without assuming that the agreement creates enforceable exclusivity.

keyTerms.meaning: The geographic or customer area described by the agreement; the actual rights and exceptions must be specified.
An operator expected to develop its own units under the agreed arrangement, rather than automatically recruiting independent subfranchisees.
Rights that can include recruiting and supporting other independent franchisees, requiring separate analysis of the actual functions.
The agreed or applicable process for addressing a default; its terms and enforceability need the relevant legal assessment.

sections.heading: The request does not prove the delivery plan
paragraphs: No U.S. unit has yet demonstrated repeat demand, local hiring or the proposed support cost. The candidate’s request may be commercially reasonable to negotiate, but home-market success and apparent capability do not establish that every requested state can be served.

Break the map into actual customer clusters, travel routes and operating bases. A centrally procured national account may still need local dispatch. An online enquiry may concern a location outside the operator’s practical service area.

sections.heading: Specify what rights are being granted
paragraphs: State who may solicit, serve and invoice national accounts, where online leads go, whether existing contracts are reserved and how cross-boundary jobs are allocated. Separate the right to open the operator’s own units from authority to recruit subfranchisees.

In a franchise structure, Item 12 is the territory-disclosure reference in the cited FTC guidance. That section does not itself create exclusivity. The May 2008 Compliance Guide is explanatory material; current federal and independent state requirements need their own application.

sections.heading: Fictional worked approach: begin with one service cluster
paragraphs: Instead of treating every requested state as equally ready, the team identifies an initial service cluster and pilot customers. It records the people, equipment, travel and support required to meet the actual customer promise. Wider rights are discussed against demonstrated demand, service quality and funded staffing.

A documented hiring, permit or procurement obstacle is different from simply ignoring a milestone. The parties need a defined adjustment process and actual agreement terms, not a rule that every delay automatically forfeits investment.

rows: Can one cluster and pilot customers be served?
Are demand, quality and staff supported?
How are customers and equipment protected?

sections.heading: Protect the brand’s support promise and the operator’s investment
paragraphs: The brand should identify what support it can fund at each stage rather than reserve a whole market indefinitely without capacity. The partner needs a realistic development timetable with objective milestones and dependencies. Record reporting, adjustment and proposed cure arrangements.

These are commercial design recommendations, not findings about enforceability. Rights against the contracting brand do not guarantee protection from independent competitors. State relationship protections and the actual agreement must be examined for the action proposed.

sections.heading: Prepare a territory principles sheet before a binding commitment
paragraphs: Show the first operating base, customer segment, service radius and evidence needed for added rights. Attach the national-account and online-lead rules so growth does not depend on informal assurances.
bullets: Separate own-unit development from subfranchise recruitment.
Map adjacent operators, reserved accounts and cross-border work.
Cost field support and travel for every stage.
Record objective milestones and reasonable delay handling.
Keep unresolved sales-law, relationship and enforceability questions visible.

practicalOutput: A territory principles sheet connecting staged rights to customer demand, service capacity, account allocation and explicit unresolved contract questions.
limitations: Fictional commercial exercise; no assurance of exclusivity or enforceability.

title: Fictional case: a Singapore subsidiary does not settle E-2 nationality
description: Trace ultimate ownership and the proposed worker’s role before relying on a treaty-country address.
learningSummary: A fictional Malaysian-owned group uses a Singapore subsidiary and assumes it can send any manager to work in the United States as a treaty business. The owner plans to stay abroad, while a technical manager may be needed for training and supervision. This example shows why company incorporation, ultimate nationality and the individual’s work must be analysed separately.

keyTerms.meaning: The treaty-investor immigration category discussed by the cited regulation; treaty listing alone does not establish eligibility.
The people at the end of the ownership chain, rather than only the immediate corporate shareholder.
The nationality question for the business under the applicable E rules, distinct from its incorporation address or tax residence.
The investment required by the relevant category, separate from simply being wealthy or holding uncommitted funds.

sections.heading: Treaty listing is a starting fact
paragraphs: The Department of State lists Singapore as an E-2 treaty country. That does not by itself establish that this enterprise or a particular person qualifies. The applicable regulation, 8 CFR 214.2(e)(7), traces enterprise ownership to ultimate individual owners as practicable.

Record incorporation, ownership percentages and ultimate nationality separately from tax residence, management control and the worker’s role. One country name on the company documents cannot answer all those questions.

sections.heading: Draw the fictional ownership chain
paragraphs: The team draws ultimate owners → Malaysian parent → Singapore subsidiary → proposed U.S. entity. It adds percentages and the facts about voting rights, director appointments and decision control. Unknown information remains unknown rather than being replaced by an assumption that all owners share the subsidiary’s nationality.

The drawing is preparation for the applicable analysis, not a visa test that automatically approves the structure. A franchise or licensing agreement is not assumed to create the corporate relationship required for a separate L-1 transfer route.

sections.heading: Describe the person’s actual U.S. activity
paragraphs: The E provisions separately address investment and whether the person acts as an investor or employee. State the proposed employer, authority, actual duties, duration and work location. A business visit, hands-on service, executive transfer and investor activity require different analysis.

Do not make the owner relocate merely because the company is expanding. If another named person is essential to launch, investigate that person’s route early. The founder staying abroad does not itself answer the manager’s eligibility.

sections.heading: Fictional worked decision: replace the assumption with two files
paragraphs: The group’s first assumption was that a Singapore company could sponsor any manager. It replaces that with an ownership file for the business and a duty-based file for the technical manager. The first shows the actual ownership and nationality facts; the second explains what work needs to happen in the United States and who employs the person.

Finance separately describes the proposed source, commitment, use and conditions of investment. Available money and a qualifying committed investment are different questions. The exercise reaches a list of unresolved requirements, not a conclusion that the manager may work.

sections.heading: Use the evidence before changing the structure or booking work
paragraphs: Check the treaty list and relevant country footnotes and the category’s enterprise and personal requirements. FAM and detailed USCIS guidance access could not be completed in the original review, so specific consular, escrow and route questions remain unresolved.

Use descriptions or aliases in the planning exercise; no passport, bank or immigration-document upload is needed. Do not reorganise ownership or commit funds just because an educational worksheet identifies an issue.
bullets: Keep ultimate nationality distinct from subsidiary country and tax residence.
Record actual ownership, control and proposed U.S. duties.
Separate capital availability from the applicable investment conditions.
Identify the unresolved individual and business questions before travel/work commitments.
Keep founder relocation optional where the founder intends to remain abroad.

practicalOutput: An ownership diagram and proposed-work description, with separate treaty, enterprise, investment and personal eligibility questions.
limitations: No visa eligibility determination.
FAM and USCIS detailed guidance access could not be completed in this review; route-specific analysis remains unresolved.

title: Fictional case: a strong branch operator is not automatically a master franchisor
description: Test the additional sales and support organisation before dividing fees or granting broad rights.
learningSummary: A fictional French services brand wants one partner to develop its U.S. network. The candidate runs branches well and asks for master rights to recruit other franchisees. This exercise separates the ability to operate company units from the ability to sell to, train and support independent owners over time.

keyTerms.meaning: A party developing its own units under the agreed arrangement.
An arrangement that can add rights and responsibilities concerning other franchisees; the actual functions and contracts matter.
The federal definition includes a party performing both the relevant pre-sale activities and post-sale performance.
The continuing staff, travel, systems and other costs of delivering the support promised to the network.

sections.heading: Start with the capability the candidate has actually demonstrated
paragraphs: The fictional candidate has strong supervisors, customer retention and multi-branch delivery. There is no evidence yet of franchise-sales administration, training independent owners or maintaining a support office. Do not treat one kind of success as proof of all those capabilities.
List the units the candidate will itself operate and the independent businesses it proposes to recruit. That distinction helps the parties understand what they are asking the new organisation to do.

sections.heading: The legal functions follow the actual arrangement
paragraphs: An own-unit developer may open its own units under a development agreement. A master arrangement can add pre-sale and post-sale responsibilities for other owners. The federal franchisor definition includes subfranchisors engaging in both kinds of activity.

Calling an arrangement development, master or licence does not decide the obligations. Definitions, exemptions and independent state requirements still need their actual analysis, including before franchise recruitment begins.

sections.heading: Compare the work before negotiating the percentage
paragraphs: Operating a branch means hiring and supervising its staff. Supporting an independent owner may require different training, problem resolution, field visits and monitoring. Recruiting employees is also different from recruiting and assessing prospective franchisees.
Write the responsibility matrix first, then cost the promised functions. A royalty split that looks generous on paper can still leave nobody funded to deliver continuing support.

rows: Handle permitted sales, disclosure and records

sections.heading: Fictional worked test: a year without new territory fees
paragraphs: The candidate and brand build an explicitly illustrative budget for staff, travel, training, localisation, systems and compliance work. They then test a year with no new territory-fee receipts. The question is whether continuing income at the planned network size can fund the support already promised.

No new earnings amount is assumed in this exercise. If the organisation relies on continually selling new rights to pay for existing obligations, the parties need to investigate that gap rather than describe the network as proven. They can revise the split, support scope, minimum funding or rollout pace.

sections.heading: Choose rights that fit the demonstrated organisation
paragraphs: A possible business decision is own-unit development first. Other possibilities are a smaller master role, building support capability before recruitment or pausing. None of those labels is a legal clearance.

Prepare one row per promised function with its responsible party, evidence of ability and annual cost. Keep initial training separate from continuing support, and test both a small network and a delayed rollout.
bullets: Name the parties contracting with each independent owner.
Identify sales, disclosure and local filing responsibilities before recruitment.
Observe owner/manager training rather than assuming branch experience is enough.
Fund continuing field and technical support.
Set the fee allocation after defining and costing the work.

practicalOutput: A responsibility-and-cost matrix showing the candidate’s own-unit work, additional master functions and a no-new-fees support test.
limitations: Commercial labels do not decide franchise-law obligations.

title: Fictional case: rent starts before the restaurant is ready to open
description: Follow the lease dates and permissions separately, then calculate the illustrative cash cost of delay.
learningSummary: A fictional restaurant operator signs a lease before confirming the premises and inspection path. Rent and other pre-opening costs can continue even when sales cannot start. This example uses invented dates and amounts to explain the cash question without forecasting a real permit delay or interpreting an actual lease.

keyTerms.meaning: When the tenant obtains the contractual access described by the lease.
The date or conditions that start the rent obligation under the actual lease.
The combination of applicable permissions and practical ability to start serving customers.
Money paid out over time, distinct from a complete accounting-profit calculation.

sections.heading: Read the fictional timetable carefully
paragraphs: Rent begins on 1 April. Fit-out is planned for two months and opening is assumed for 1 June. The team has not confirmed permitted use, design requirements or the inspection sequence. These are deliberately invented teaching assumptions, with no real address or local-law claim.

The lease establishes payment obligations according to its actual terms. Relevant authorities establish operating permissions under applicable rules. A landlord’s assurance cannot simply be substituted for the latter.

sections.heading: Separate rent from the other occupancy amounts
paragraphs: Read each commercial lease rather than assuming it is triple-net, that taxes are included or that other charges follow a universal percentage. Record deposits, taxes, insurance, maintenance, utilities and reconciliations where the actual agreement provides for them.

The same care applies to works and access: possession, ability to survey or fit out, rent commencement and opening may be different dates. A property schedule should show them separately so finance knows what can be paid before revenue starts.

sections.heading: Calculate only what the fictional delay assumptions support
paragraphs: Assume $8,000 per month of base rent and a separately identified $6,000 per month for pre-opening staff/utilities. If a three-month opening delay occurs while both continue, that adds $42,000 of cash use: $14,000 × 3.

That amount excludes debt, extra fit-out, spoilage and other charges. It is neither a permit-delay prediction nor the total project funding requirement. The narrow calculation is useful precisely because its inclusions and exclusions are visible.

rows: Access for survey, works and storage
Actual tax, insurance, maintenance, utilities and deposit terms
When service and collection can begin

sections.heading: Fictional worked response: change the sequence before further spending
paragraphs: The project lead replaces the single opening date with the tasks that must precede it: use confirmation, design, landlord approval, works, inspections, utilities and the food-operation questions. The team identifies which missing answer could change the site or equipment choice.

SBA’s licensing guidance explains that requirements depend on activity and location. A real project therefore needs the actual municipality, county, address, use and sector before relying on a local route. The fictional exercise cannot supply those answers.

sections.heading: Make the lease and cash schedules talk to each other
paragraphs: Abstract the actual payment and improvement terms, any conditions or extension rights and who must resolve them. Keep landlord, insurer and authority documents separate according to what each proves. Link each delay scenario to monthly payments, avoiding the same rent being counted in both fit-out and an additional reserve.
Management can investigate conditions, timing, another site, staged spending or a pause. The example approves none of those options for a real contract.
bullets: Record the actual payment and access clauses.
Identify permissions that depend on the chosen address.
Name responsibility for each prerequisite and supporting document.
Model cash until customer receipts begin.
Keep assumed delays separate from authority-provided dates.

practicalOutput: A lease-date and permissions schedule linked to an explicitly labelled monthly delay scenario.
limitations: No named locality researched by this scenario.
Delay assumptions are fictional; lease interpretation and actual local approvals remain unresolved.

title: Fictional case: the home-market cleaning product needs a U.S. supply decision
description: Separate pesticide status, importing, the producing establishment and actual product use.
learningSummary: A fictional Singapore cleaning brand wants its U.S. partner to use the same disinfectant bottle as at home. For this exercise only, the product is assumed to be a FIFRA-regulated pesticide. A real product needs its own classification and supply analysis; no actual formula, registration or permission is identified here.

keyTerms.meaning: The federal pesticide law relevant to the assumed product category in this exercise.
A product purpose assessed through the applicable claims, ingredient and knowledge tests, not only one word on its label.
A record concerning the establishment; it is not product approval.
The EPA shipment paperwork discussed for the applicable import route.
The combined supply cost including the relevant shipping, entry, handling, storage and compliance amounts.

sections.heading: A real product needs more than the fictional assumption
paragraphs: The case assumes a regulated pesticide so the team can examine that supply problem. For a real cleaner, deodoriser or bleach, section 152.10 contains nonpesticidal-purpose/claim conditions. Section 152.15 also considers claims or implications in labelling or elsewhere, ingredients with no other significant commercially valuable use, and actual or constructive knowledge of pesticidal intended use.

That means the assessment can look beyond a familiar formula, foreign approval or the absence of a single word. Keep the actual composition, label, website/sales claims, intended sites/uses and supporting record together.

sections.heading: Product status and import paperwork do different jobs
paragraphs: EPA’s import guidance distinguishes lawful product status, producing-establishment requirements and Notice of Arrival paperwork. An establishment number does not approve the product. Foreign sale does not permit an unregistered pesticide to be imported for ordinary U.S. use; specific exceptions have their own conditions.

Establish the actual product, use and import route, including the applicable Notice of Arrival timing before arrival. Product/import records also do not replace applicator or business authorisations, worker requirements or state/client-use conditions.

sections.heading: Fictional worked comparison: lawful import or a suitable U.S. substitute
paragraphs: Operations and the responsible technical team investigate two routes: establish a lawful import/supply path for the specified product, or validate an appropriate U.S. substitute. They compare intended use, label directions, application method, surface compatibility, client specification, training, storage and continuity.

A familiar smell or bottle colour does not define the cleaning result the customer needs. A substitute may change stock logistics without automatically resolving all product and applicator requirements. No real product is declared suitable or authorised in this exercise.

sections.heading: Do not make missing costs disappear
paragraphs: Use a transparent worksheet for purchase cost, freight, insurance, customs/broker costs, applicable duties/tariffs, local handling, storage and compliance. Record currency, quantity, unit, quote date and importer. If a duty rate is unknown, the total is incomplete rather than zero.
Minimum orders and delivery times also affect the cash schedule. A low bottle price can be an incomplete comparison if it omits inventory funding or other responsibilities.

rows: Actual importer and lawful product status
Composition, claims, label and supply record
Complete landed cost and stock funding

sections.heading: Prepare a supply specification for investigation
paragraphs: The output is not a declaration that a product may enter or be used. It should identify the exact product and claims, the responsible importer/supplier/operator, the records still needed and the proposed performance comparison.
Update the operating manual only after the actual technical and compliance decisions are supported.
bullets: Keep category uncertain until the actual facts establish it.
Separate product, establishment, shipment and user permissions.
Document each party’s supply responsibility.
Keep missing tariffs and costs visible.
Test a substitute against objective use and compatibility criteria.

practicalOutput: A product-and-supply comparison identifying classification, import responsibilities, complete cost inputs and the evidence still needed before use.
limitations: No actual EPA product determination, import authorisation or current tariff calculation.

title: Burgerim: understand the entity default judgment and its limits
description: A real historical judgment connects franchise-sales promises with the evidence and support behind them.
learningSummary: An expanding brand may delegate U.S. sales to a separate team, but someone still needs to own the evidence behind its promises. This real Burgerim example explains a January 2024 judgment against identified companies. It keeps the court’s orders separate from actual collection, later court activity and the consequences for a different business.

keyTerms.meaning: A company or other legal entity named as a defendant, distinct from an individual person.
A judgment following a party’s default, rather than a contested trial of the merits.
The relief amount ordered for consumers in the identified judgment; ordering it does not prove distribution.
An optional business record connecting each proposed statement to its supporting facts, responsible person and approved use; it is not a prescribed legal form.

sections.heading: Identify the particular judgment
paragraphs: On 19 January 2024, the Central District of California entered default judgment against Burgerim Group USA, Inc. and Burgerim Group, Inc. The order followed their default; it was not a contested merits trial. Page 3 separately notes an earlier order as to Oren Loni.

The entity order bars those entity defendants from U.S. franchise sales and imposes $7,750,000 in civil penalties and $48,476,689 for consumer redress. Keep the identity of the parties and the order clear rather than treating all references to the case as the same decision.

sections.heading: A judgment amount is different from money recovered
paragraphs: These are judgments entered, not evidence that the money was collected or paid to buyers. The FTC case index still carries a Pending label and a January 2024 last-update date. That index description does not supply a complete current docket.

This article reviews the identified historical entity order. It does not state a recovery rate, certify every later development or make a present-conduct finding about a current business. Nor does it offer an automatic penalty formula for another violation.

sections.heading: The order connects numbers with support promises
paragraphs: The order addresses misrepresentations about income, payback time, training, assistance and other material facts. Material facts are the important facts relevant to the transaction. For a brand owner, the lesson is that a promise of support needs an actual person, resource and delivery plan behind it.

A sales team may be external or geographically distant, but that does not make the evidence question disappear. Keep financial statements, opening-time claims and service promises connected to what the organisation can actually support.

sections.heading: Fictional exercise: examine one proposed opening statement
paragraphs: Imagine a fictional brand proposes saying its new U.S. partners can open quickly. The team separates site choice, customer procurement, fit-out, permissions and staffing. It then asks which parts of the statement the available evidence actually supports.

For a training or support statement, it names the team, travel budget and response capacity. These are original business-planning questions, not further findings about Burgerim. No new case fact or financial outcome is assumed.

sections.heading: Give every sales statement an evidence owner
paragraphs: Before materials or scripts are used, record each claim, its author, supporting facts, audience, approved form and review date. Retain the brochure, website, slides and spoken-script version that was actually approved.

A private calculator for evaluating your model is different from an approved earnings statement to a prospective franchisee. Use the current federal and state requirements for today’s sale; the historical judgment does not replace them.
bullets: State exactly what the evidence supports and where it stops.
Assign support delivery to funded, named roles.
Record complaints and refund obligations against the actual contract.
Keep ordered money separate from verified collection.
Review current rules independently before using prospect-facing claims.

practicalOutput: A written record of proposed sales promises, connecting financial, opening and support statements to supporting facts, responsible people and current requirements.
limitations: Historical entity judgment only; no recovery proof or full current docket certification.
The case does not establish automatic sanctions for every violation.

title: Tower Cleaning: a historical settlement about earnings claims and records
description: Learn from the identified 1996 decree without treating old disclosure rules as today’s FDD instructions.
learningSummary: A commercial-cleaning brand can show substantial customer billings without demonstrating what an operator earns after delivery costs. This real historical case connects earnings statements with supporting records. Its consent decree provides a bounded lesson, while the following planning exercise is separate from the actual case facts.

keyTerms.meaning: A court settlement document whose admissions and obligations must be read from its actual terms.
Uniform Franchise Offering Circular, the earlier disclosure framework referenced in this historical decree.
Franchise Disclosure Document, the current disclosure-document term; current requirements must be examined separately.
The defined group of accounts or units used for a comparison, including its period and exclusions.

sections.heading: What the reviewed decree establishes
paragraphs: The official FTC record for Tower Cleaning Systems, Inc. and David A. Gansky links a 1996 consent decree in the Middle District of Pennsylvania. It says the settlement occurred without adjudication of disputed issues and without admission of liability. That is different from a contested finding or an admitted violation.

The decree includes $50,000 consumer redress and restrictions on misrepresenting franchise sales, income or profits. Those are its terms, not proof that the money was collected. No later-operation or complete later-docket finding is made here.

sections.heading: Understand the date of the disclosure references
paragraphs: The reviewed decree and appendices use the pre-2007 Franchise Rule and UFOC framework for the disclosure and earnings-document references. Those historical requirements are not instructions for preparing a current FDD.

The useful connection is between a sales claim and the records supporting it. Apply today’s independent rules to a proposed statement rather than assuming that following a historical order’s wording meets the present requirements.

sections.heading: Why gross account billings do not explain the operator’s result
paragraphs: For a cleaning business, the customer’s contract amount does not identify labour hours, travel between buildings, rework, supplies, churn or payment delay. Moving an account portfolio to another operator can also change staffing and route density.

These are original business-analysis questions, not extra findings about Tower. They matter because a comparison can look favourable while describing an operation with different costs or owner participation from the one being offered.

sections.heading: Fictional exercise: compare accounts on a consistent basis
paragraphs: A fictional cleaning brand prepares an account comparison for its first U.S. partner model. Before adding figures, it defines the period, area, service mix, unit age and owner/manager involvement. It records lost or excluded accounts and explains why they are outside the group.

It then separates contracted revenue, invoiced revenue and cash received, and records site time, travel, supervision, equipment and quality costs. No invented profit result is supplied. The point is to establish what each record actually represents rather than call a hand-selected group typical.

sections.heading: Make the record usable before making the claim
paragraphs: Prepare a worksheet with a source and reviewer next to each number. Keep one-unit and combined-operation information distinct and retain the definitions and exclusions used in the comparison.

This supports an internal business decision; it is not itself an authorised financial performance representation. Proposed prospect-facing statements need the current FDD/rule review. The historical settlement is a lesson about evidence, not a finding that your business has the same conduct or outcome.
bullets: Separate contracted sales, invoices and actual cash.
Define the comparison group before selecting results.
Record owner/manager participation and delivery costs.
Explain exclusions and material differences.
Preserve the source, calculation, approved statement and its limits.

practicalOutput: An account-comparison worksheet defining costs, owner involvement, exclusions and source records, kept separate from current prospect-facing disclosures.
limitations: Historical consent resolution without admission; current rules require separate analysis.
No payment or current-business finding is made.

title: Qargo Coffee: what the FTC alleged about a licence-labelled offer
description: A real historical complaint and settlement reports illustrate why the operating facts matter more than the agreement’s name.
learningSummary: A brand may describe a U.S. relationship as a licence or distributorship while providing rights and support that still need franchise analysis. This Qargo Coffee article explains the actual historical records reviewed. It distinguishes the complaint’s allegations from reported settlement status and leaves final remedy terms unstated because the signed entered order was not obtained.

keyTerms.meaning: The document stating the agency’s allegations; it is not itself a contested-trial finding.
An order based on an agreement, whose actual entry and terms must be established from the relevant record.
The Federal Trade Commission, the U.S. agency that brought the complaint.
Applying the relevant definition and then considering exemptions and independent state requirements from the actual relationship.

sections.heading: Identify the allegation and the document
paragraphs: The FTC filed its complaint on 16 October 2024 in the Southern District of Florida. It alleged that Qargo Coffee’s California offering used distributorship and affiliated-licence language while operating as a franchise. Paragraphs 26–35 describe the brand, fees, controls and support facts on which the agency relied.

Those are allegations, not findings from a contested trial. The useful lesson for another brand is to identify the actual rights, payments and operating relationship, not to assume that the same outcome applies whenever a contract uses the word licence.

sections.heading: The official reports establish a bounded settlement account
paragraphs: The FTC’s December 2024 litigation report records entry of a stipulated order on 17 October 2024. A later report to Congress covering fiscal 2025 lists the matter as Full Settlement. Those records support the historical settlement description.

They do not establish collection, current compliance or the absence of other disputes. The FTC index still uses a Pending label and links a proposed order. A stale index label should not be treated as proof that settlement never occurred, but it also does not supply a complete current court record.

sections.heading: Why this article does not state the final remedies
paragraphs: The reviewed material does not include the actual signed entered order. The page therefore does not recite final monetary, rescission or noncompete terms. A proposed document cannot silently stand in for the entered order.

Keep the different questions separate: what the FTC alleged, what official reports say happened, what the entered order required and whether anyone performed or paid. Only the supported parts are stated here. No present-conduct, recovery or complete-docket conclusion is made.

sections.heading: Apply the lesson to the relationship being offered
paragraphs: The current federal framework examines trademark association, significant operating control or assistance, and a required payment or commitment. Exemptions and state requirements remain separate questions. Neither a licence label nor one operating requirement automatically settles the whole analysis.

The May 2008 FTC Compliance Guide is explanatory guidance, not current law or a current threshold sheet. Use it here to understand distinctions such as trademark protection versus broader operating directions, while relying on current authorities for the actual legal test.

sections.heading: Fictional exercise: describe what the operator receives and owes
paragraphs: Imagine a fictional service brand gives a partner brand rights, training and mandatory systems in return for fees. The expansion lead records who receives payment, what support is promised, how standards are enforced and who contracts with customers. Spoken sales promises belong in the record as well as the draft agreement.

The team then identifies seller, buyer, offer and proposed-operation locations and the factual assumptions needing confirmation. This is an original preparation exercise, not a further allegation about Qargo or a verdict on the fictional arrangement.
bullets: Record brand rights, payment recipients and timing.
Describe actual training, systems, assistance and enforcement rights.
Retain drafts, presentations and relevant sales promises.
Analyse federal definitions/exemptions and state requirements separately.
Leave final-order remedies and current status unresolved until the actual supporting records are read.

practicalOutput: A relationship description showing actual rights, fees, controls, support and locations, with the historical complaint and settlement limits kept explicit.
limitations: Actual signed final-order terms remain unreviewed and are not stated.
No present conduct, money-recovery or complete current-docket finding is made.

title: Commercial cleaning: build the first U.S. operation around accounts and routes
description: Test the customer contract, staffing, supervision and cash collection before assuming a local manager can run the model.
learningSummary: For an established cleaning company, the useful operating unit may be a cluster of customer accounts rather than a shop. A U.S. partner needs enough nearby work, appropriate staff and management, and money to pay costs before customers pay. This guide explains how to investigate that practical model without treating home-market success as proof of U.S. demand.

keyTerms.meaning: How closely accounts and service times fit together, affecting travel, staffing and supervision.
The customer’s process for selecting a supplier and agreeing the work.
Amounts invoiced to customers but not yet collected.
Dependence on a small number of customers, so losing one can materially affect the operation.

sections.heading: Define the account cluster before the territory
paragraphs: Compare customer types, usable service hours, site access, journey times, frequency and contract length. A contract that works well in the home market demonstrates delivery there; it does not establish U.S. labour availability, customer demand or procurement acceptance.
Identify the supervisor’s practical area and what happens when accounts have conflicting service windows. A large geographic territory is not a substitute for a workable route.

sections.heading: A manager does not remove the other management jobs
paragraphs: Assign who estimates labour, wins bids, covers absences, responds to complaints and collects invoices. Price dedicated management and quality supervision before assuming a royalty is affordable. If the overseas founder still performs those jobs, that dependence needs to be visible.

Test customer concentration separately. Losing one large building can remove revenue while supervisory time, vehicles and route gaps remain. A broad sales forecast may hide that account-specific problem.

sections.heading: Separate workplace duties from customer purchasing conditions
paragraphs: OSHA, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, identifies cleaning-industry chemical, equipment and workplace hazards and links applicable general-industry standards. The responsible employer needs an actual task/product safety review. This page does not establish safety clearance for a particular job.

A customer may also require insurance evidence, background screening or a particular service level. Record those as customer purchasing conditions unless independently required by law. Identify their source and cost rather than treating every requested document as a government licence.

sections.heading: Fictional example: investigate three nearby office buildings
paragraphs: A fictional brand investigates three nearby buildings instead of assuming a national rollout. For each, it records the bid process, service times, access, equipment storage, staffing cover, customer sign-off and collection terms. Missing travel or wage information remains missing, rather than improving the market score.

The team asks whether one supervisor can support the actual schedule and who replaces an absent worker. Finance follows invoice acceptance, disputes and expected receipts alongside payroll. The exercise produces questions and evidence requirements, not invented margins or a successful pilot result.

sections.heading: Use the customer’s payment terms in the cash plan
paragraphs: Contracted revenue, an accepted invoice and money received are different events. SBA’s finance guidance is a useful accounting reference; the operator needs its own dated costs and collections to see the funding requirement. A profitable annual estimate does not show whether the next payroll can be met.

For national accounts, record who receives the work, which operator serves each site and who invoices. A paid pilot must be arranged lawfully; evidence from delivery does not itself authorise offers of franchise rights.

sections.heading: Prepare the next bid as a repeatable management process
paragraphs: Create an account-level brief that operations and finance can both use. Keep the customer’s renewal and termination provisions with the service and cash assumptions.
bullets: Record the customer, tender date and actual contract conditions.
Map service hours, travel, supervision and cover.
Separate legal duties from customer and insurer conditions.
Track invoice approval, disputes and actual cash dates.
Define national-account allocation and lawful pilot responsibilities.

practicalOutput: An account-level pilot brief showing the route, staffing, customer conditions, management duties and invoice-to-cash timing.
limitations: No location-specific wage, tax, customer demand or safety clearance.

title: Facilities services: split the customer bundle into actual jobs
description: One contract can contain several trades, subcontractors and cash responsibilities.
learningSummary: A facilities brand may promise a customer one point of contact for cleaning, repairs, landscaping and other services. That is convenient commercially, but each underlying activity still needs the right operator and any applicable permission. The brand and local partner should define both who delivers the work and who pays for it while waiting for the customer.

keyTerms.meaning: The contract’s performance requirements, such as response, completion evidence, exclusions and credits.
A separate business engaged to deliver part of the customer service; its role does not automatically settle the main contractor’s duties.
A contractual adjustment associated with the agreed service terms, to be read from the actual contract.
The customer’s process for accepting the invoiced work, which can affect when money is received.

sections.heading: Describe each activity inside the facilities promise
paragraphs: List cleaning, planned maintenance, access systems, pest control, landscaping, repairs and any other work actually included. Record what the partner performs, subcontracts or only coordinates. A facilities brand licence does not itself authorise every task.

State the worksite and contracting/employing business. Professional, contractor and sector requirements can affect which business may deliver a particular service and what it must retain or supervise.

sections.heading: The customer contract needs named operating responsibilities
paragraphs: A service-level agreement can cover response time, completion evidence, exclusions, escalation and credits. Decide who dispatches, approves extra work, invoices, responds to emergencies and bears rework costs. A single sales promise may need several teams behind it.

Customers may require specific insurance, references or approved subcontractors. Keep those purchasing conditions distinct from government and insurer requirements so the operator understands their actual source and price.

sections.heading: Investigate permissions by activity and location
paragraphs: SBA, the U.S. Small Business Administration, directs businesses to licensing requirements according to their activities and locations. Begin with the actual state, municipality, county and site rather than assuming a universal facilities-services licence.

A subcontractor’s own licence does not automatically resolve all obligations of the main contracting or employing business. Identify the authority and actual question for each job. This article provides a planning method, not a permission for the whole bundle.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a multi-site customer pays on 60-day terms
paragraphs: A fictional partner wins a multi-site customer with 60-day invoice terms. It must pay technicians and subcontractors earlier, while the customer can dispute work if completion evidence is missing. The financial question therefore includes both gross margin and dated cash collection.

The team follows a job from dispatch to customer sign-off, invoice and payment, recording who fixes missing evidence. It also tests the effect of that national customer failing or withholding payment separately from a broad market-sales percentage. The 60 days are fictional contract terms, not a statutory deadline or an actual customer result.

sections.heading: Price the coordination, not just the technician’s visit
paragraphs: Include emergency cover, subcontractor selection and management, reporting, rework and any agreed credits. If a job crosses an operator’s territory, specify who may accept it, deliver it and invoice it. An informal understanding can leave both support and cash costs unclear.

SBA’s finance guidance supports the distinction between accounting and cash questions; the actual contract and receipts determine the model’s inputs. Do not claim a complete funding answer from a quoted margin alone.

sections.heading: Build a service-by-service table before the full offer is promised
paragraphs: For each task show the worksite, contracting business, employer, delivery lead, subcontractor if any, relevant public authority and customer conditions. Add response, evidence and payment responsibilities. This suggested table makes the one-contact promise understandable to the people who must deliver it.
bullets: Separate performed, subcontracted and coordinated services.
Identify the actual permission question and responsible party.
Record customer and insurer conditions separately from law.
Price emergency response, rework and coordination.
Connect national-account allocation to invoice and cash timing.

practicalOutput: A service-by-service table showing delivery, permissions, customer conditions, performance responsibilities and payment timing.
limitations: No universal facilities-services licence analysis.

title: Pest control: connect the product, applicator and operating jurisdiction
description: A U.S. product source and an experienced overseas team do not settle every local permission.
learningSummary: A pest-control brand can provide a method and recurring customer contracts, but the U.S. operator needs appropriately authorised people and products for the actual work. Federal certification is a starting point, with state, territorial and tribal administration and potentially broader commercial requirements. Build those facts into route and staffing plans before promising coverage.

keyTerms.meaning: The product category for which the cited EPA guidance explains applicator/supervisor certification requirements.
The relevant qualification for applying or supervising the covered pesticide work, distinct from product status.
An operating permission for the business where required, separate from an individual’s certification.
A return service visit, which affects the capacity and cost of the recurring route.

sections.heading: Start with the treatment rather than the territory map
paragraphs: List the target pest, treatment method, site, product and people applying or supervising it. Separate the product’s lawful status, the individual’s certification and any business licence. Home-country training may demonstrate experience, but does not itself establish U.S. authority.
The same service description can need different answers in different places or categories. Identify those questions before assigning the technician or assuming the brand manual is sufficient.

sections.heading: Understand the federal starting point and local administration
paragraphs: EPA, the Environmental Protection Agency, explains certification for restricted-use pesticide applicators or supervisors under the relevant rules. State, territorial and tribal authorities administer certification. Many states have broader requirements for commercial work.

Check each actual operating jurisdiction and category. Do not assume certification automatically travels across a state boundary. This page does not decide a particular state certificate, supervision arrangement or product authorisation.

sections.heading: Importing and applying are different responsibilities
paragraphs: If the brand proposes importing a familiar treatment, identify the actual product, importer and applicable product/establishment and arrival requirements. EPA’s import guidance does not turn a foreign approval into permission for ordinary U.S. use. The applicable exceptions and shipment route require their actual conditions.

Using a U.S.-sourced product may change stock logistics but does not erase applicator or business requirements. Keep product, person, business and jurisdiction records connected without treating one as proof of the others.

sections.heading: Fictional example: two neighbouring states are not one permission
paragraphs: A fictional European brand proposes importing a treatment and starting in two neighbouring states. The team divides the investigation into lawful product/import supply and each state’s people/business requirements. For each proposed job, it records the relevant site, product use, person and supervision question.

It then compares a U.S. supply option against the actual service specification. The exercise grants no import permission or certification. It shows why a convenient bottle source and a nearby state border do not settle the operating plan.

sections.heading: Make route economics reflect the actual service
paragraphs: Recurring accounts can improve route density, but callbacks, emergencies, seasonal demand, product storage and access conditions affect capacity. A very wide territory can consume supervisory travel time. Record actual customer insurance requests and spill, vehicle and product-use responsibilities rather than treating an insurance quote as approval.
Price the qualified supervision and backup needed for the first market before assuming a royalty is affordable. Unsupported certificate, fee, coverage or demand inputs should remain unresolved.
bullets: Record products and label-directed sites/uses.
Name the certifying authority and category for each area.
Identify qualified people and required supervision.
Assign storage, transport, notice and incident questions.
Collect evidence for seasonality, travel and callbacks.

practicalOutput: A product/person/business/jurisdiction table linked to route capacity, supervision and the unresolved launch requirements.
limitations: No state certification or specific product conclusion.

title: Industrial maintenance: prove the delivery behind a response promise
description: Customer qualification, hazardous-energy duties and specialist cover belong in the first-market plan.
learningSummary: An industrial-maintenance brand may be judged on how quickly it can restore a customer’s operation. The U.S. partner therefore needs to establish the precise work, qualified people and customer access conditions before selling broad coverage. This guide connects those practical decisions with the limited hazardous-energy starting point and the costs of specialist response.

keyTerms.meaning: The customer’s process for deciding which suppliers and people it will accept for the work.
The energy risks in servicing and maintenance addressed by the cited OSHA overview and applicable standard.
The people and arrangements available to respond outside ordinary scheduled work.
A contractually defined consequence of the agreed service terms, to be checked in the actual contract.

sections.heading: Define the equipment and work before the brand promise
paragraphs: Industrial maintenance can include inspection, machine servicing, electrical tasks and process-critical repair. State the equipment and boundaries of the job, who can approve an exception and when specialists must be called. A broad maintenance description does not establish permission for every activity.
Customer engineering approval, site access and procurement can also determine whether the partner can deliver. Record those conditions separately from public professional or trade requirements.

sections.heading: Hazardous-energy duties need actual task assessment
paragraphs: OSHA, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, explains hazardous-energy risks in servicing/maintenance and points to 29 CFR 1910.147. For covered work, the responsible employer needs appropriate energy-control procedures and training.

Identify the real task and host/contractor interface. This overview does not decide exemptions or replace the customer-site procedure. Construction, maritime, State Plan and particular trade questions need their own applicable analysis; a brand checklist is not an actual safe-work determination.

sections.heading: Translate response time into people, travel and resources
paragraphs: A four-hour response promise is a staffing, geography and spare-parts decision. Identify on-call pay, specialist cover, travel, calibration, tools, insurance and subcontractors before pricing it. Do not assume the same technician can meet every overlapping call.

A customer’s production-loss exposure is different from the service fee. Liability terms and service credits belong in the actual contract and financial review. No universal allocation or insurance adequacy is established here.

sections.heading: Fictional example: investigate one industrial corridor
paragraphs: A fictional Dutch brand chooses one corridor for customer interviews and a lawfully arranged pilot. It asks what a supplier must demonstrate before bidding, how shutdown work is scheduled and who approves a new technician. The team describes the actual equipment and potential demand rather than using a national population total as evidence.

It then tests the proposed response promise against dispatch, specialist availability, travel and parts. Missing information remains a question to resolve, not an assumed successful pilot or financial result. The exercise does not authorise a task or replace site procedures.

sections.heading: Compare recurring contracts with shutdown projects
paragraphs: Recurring maintenance income and one-off shutdown jobs can create different capacity and cash requirements. Record their staffing, customer approval and collection conditions separately. SBA’s finance material is a reference for the accounting/cash distinction, not a source of actual U.S. margins.
The support organisation must also be funded without assuming repeated territory-sale fees. A large territory grant cannot make a sparse customer base or missing specialist capacity disappear.

sections.heading: Prepare the first-corridor brief
paragraphs: Show assets and tasks, competent people, customer purchasing/safety/insurance conditions and the relevant local trade questions. Give technical escalation and backup clear owners.
bullets: Define what the partner performs and when work is referred.
Identify the actual customer qualification process.
Build the required task-specific safety and training arrangements.
Test response time with supported travel, staff and parts assumptions.
Separate recurring, project and continuing-support costs.

practicalOutput: A first-corridor brief showing exact tasks, qualified delivery, customer conditions and the resources needed for the response promise.
limitations: Task-specific OSHA, state-plan and trade scope remains to be reviewed.

title: Technical services: find the decisions that still depend on the founder
description: Test whether another manager can use the method, recognise its limits and obtain qualified help.
learningSummary: A technical company can have branch managers while its founder still decides every unusual quotation, fault or warranty dispute. That dependence can become expensive when a U.S. partner works in a different time zone. Before granting broad rights, identify the decisions, authorisations and support resources needed to deliver without constant owner intervention.

keyTerms.meaning: Referring a question to a person with the required authority or expertise.
Observed work, training and stated limits supporting a person’s ability, rather than an automatic professional licence.
A customer’s acceptance requirements, distinct from government authority.
A suggested table naming who may decide what, when to refer it and who provides backup.

sections.heading: List the exceptions the founder handles
paragraphs: Record unusual jobs, specifications, supplier substitutions, pricing decisions and warranty disputes. For each, note frequency, required response time and the consequence of a wrong or late decision.

A general independence score cannot show whether those decisions have transferred. The useful evidence is what a proposed manager can actually do using the documentation, and where the method still requires another qualified person.

sections.heading: Experience and legal authority are separate questions
paragraphs: Divide tasks into inspection, advice, design, installation, repair or certification. Requirements depend on the actual activity, state, profession and site. SBA’s licensing-by-activity/location approach is a starting point, not a professional credential decision.

A foreign qualification or brand licence does not settle U.S. authority. Equally, customer accreditation or acceptance requirements should not be mistaken for government permission. Record the actual source and conditions of each requirement.

sections.heading: Price the technical decision channel
paragraphs: Include quotation help, complex faults, documentation, audits and customer meetings in the support budget. If a U.S. manager must wait overnight for the European founder, a customer response promise can fail even when the field staff are capable.

Name the primary and backup decision makers and distinguish the brand, partner and appropriately authorised professional roles. Cost remote support and necessary visits instead of treating the founder’s continuing effort as free.

sections.heading: Fictional example: work through ten past exception jobs
paragraphs: A fictional German testing-services brand selects ten historic exception jobs with sanitised information. A proposed manager records the decision they would make, what information is missing and when they would escalate. The responsible technical lead compares the reasoning with the method and its limits.

The team uses disagreements to identify unclear documentation or missing support. It then tests the revised process on the defined exercise. This does not confer professional competence, predict future outcomes or approve actual testing work. No confidential customer details need to be inserted into the learning exercise.

sections.heading: Keep the business choice narrower than the ambition
paragraphs: A bounded U.S. pilot can investigate whether the manager, support channel and customer requirements fit together before broad rights are granted. State what the pilot is intended to test and which actual permissions must already be established.

SBA finance guidance is a useful reference when separating operating costs and cash questions. It does not provide the missing wage, travel or support quote. Keep those inputs tied to the real proposed organisation.

sections.heading: Prepare a decision-and-support table
paragraphs: Give every founder-only decision a proposed local owner, permitted limits, evidence and backup. Record which decisions must remain with the brand or an appropriately authorised person rather than insisting that every task becomes local.
bullets: Map technical, pricing and customer exceptions.
Name qualified primary and backup decision makers.
Retain training and observed-performance evidence.
Separate customer acceptance from government authorisation.
Cost support and define the actual pilot before wider grants.

practicalOutput: A decision-and-support table showing local authority, limits, evidence, escalation and backup for work previously owned by the founder.
limitations: No professional credential or regulatory approval is issued.

title: IT services: decide who gets access and who responds when something goes wrong
description: Connect the customer, partner and overseas support team before promising continuous service.
learningSummary: An IT-services brand may deliver through a U.S. partner while specialist support stays overseas. Customers need to know who may access their systems, approve changes and act on an incident. The operating plan should connect those responsibilities with the staffing and supplier commitments behind the service promise.

keyTerms.meaning: Ongoing support or operation of agreed customer systems, whose actual duties must be described in the contract.
The U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, which provides the small-business cybersecurity guidance cited here.
An event needing the relevant security response; the actual legal and contractual reporting duties must be determined separately.
Removing or changing access when a worker or business relationship ends.

sections.heading: Draw the actual service and access relationships
paragraphs: IT support, software implementation, managed services and training need different access. Record who contracts with the customer, whose staff access systems, where access occurs, what data is involved and who authorises changes.

Brand software rights, the customer’s own licence and permission to access a system are different things. A partner’s right to use the brand does not answer what customer information its technicians may see or change.

sections.heading: Use cybersecurity guidance for the role it actually plays
paragraphs: NIST offers small-business guidance on cybersecurity risks, incident response, cloud security and related topics. Use it as a preparation reference. It is not a universal law, a service endorsement or certification of the proposed business.

Actual customer contracts, public contracts, sector requirements and privacy law need their own evidence and applicability assessment. Keep a recommended internal control distinct from a specific legal obligation.

sections.heading: Make the support hours affordable and deliverable
paragraphs: A U.S. customer may need service while the parent team sleeps. Price on-call cover, specialist escalation, third-party licences, secure onboarding/offboarding, backups, incident exercises and reporting. A 24/7 promise needs the people and supplier commitments behind it.

Decide who may approve emergency work, who funds it and who may communicate externally about an incident. Record applicable contractual and legal deadlines without inventing one reporting period for all customers and incidents.

sections.heading: Fictional example: rehearse before granting live customer access
paragraphs: A fictional Southeast Asian managed-service brand gives one U.S. partner a limited support role. In a test environment, the teams rehearse removing a departed technician’s access and responding to a suspicious-login report.

They record who receives the report, who can make the relevant changes, how the overseas team is reached and what happens if it is unavailable. The result is evidence of an exercise, not proof of legal compliance, a secure real system or absence of risk. No actual customer data is required for this learning task.

sections.heading: Turn the rehearsal into a usable operating document
paragraphs: Prepare an access-and-incident responsibility schedule showing customer, brand and partner entities, actual data paths, named approvers and the access needed for each role. Limiting access to the work needed is a practical design recommendation here, not a universal legal determination.

Keep cross-border privacy and sector restrictions unresolved until assessed. Supplier licences, security services and customer-specific cover need actual cost assumptions. SBA finance guidance can support the accounting approach but does not supply those quotes.

sections.heading: Prepare for either business being unavailable
paragraphs: Test how support continues if the parent or partner cannot respond. The goal is to understand the dependency before a customer relies on the promise.
bullets: Record actual systems, data, locations and staff access.
Name access approvers and removal responsibilities.
Assign incident, customer and supplier communications.
Record actual applicable deadlines rather than one universal period.
Budget and test backup cover for the promised service window.

practicalOutput: An access-and-incident schedule linking systems, people, approvals, communication and backup cover to the actual customer promise.
limitations: No comprehensive federal/state or cross-border privacy assessment.

title: Business training: explain what the learner’s certificate actually means
description: Separate course rights and teaching capability from occupational or education permission.
learningSummary: A training brand may offer corporate workshops, technical instruction or courses advertised as a route into an occupation. Those services do not all raise the same questions. The expanding business should define what learners receive, what rights a partner can use and what another instructor can actually deliver before selling a standard programme.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidence of attendance; it is different from a licence to practise or a recognised professional qualification.
A credential issued under the brand’s own system, whose meaning must be stated accurately.
The rights governing use of the materials, software, recordings, marks and translations.
How much of the realistically available teaching capacity is actually used for paid work.

sections.heading: Describe the learning service and the promised outcome
paragraphs: Distinguish corporate workshops, technical instruction, assessment and a course marketed as qualifying someone for an occupation. State what the learner receives and who recognises it. An attendance certificate, private brand credential, occupational licence and recognised qualification are different records.

This matters to both sales audiences. The prospective partner needs to understand what it may deliver and promise; the learner or corporate customer needs an accurate description of the course and credential.

sections.heading: Investigate the actual activity and location
paragraphs: SBA’s general licensing guidance connects requirements with business activity and operating location. Record where teaching, student recruitment, assessment and customer contracting occur. Licensing a syllabus does not itself establish authority for all those activities.

If the offer touches a regulated occupation, childcare, healthcare or postsecondary education, investigate the relevant requirements before making sales promises. This article does not determine a professional or education exemption or approval.

sections.heading: Give the partner usable content and instructor rights
paragraphs: Record who owns and may use the slides, software, recordings, marks, learner materials and translations. Identify who updates technical content and who approves instructors. A curriculum can become unusable if the agreement does not provide the actual delivery rights.

A successful home-market branch may also depend on the founder’s teaching or reputation. Observe whether another instructor can deliver the defined outcome using the materials and stated assessment criteria, rather than assuming a training manual replaces that capability.

sections.heading: Fictional example: follow one paid corporate workshop
paragraphs: A fictional European business-to-business training brand tests one paid corporate workshop through a properly reviewed arrangement. It records customer procurement, instructor preparation, venue/platform cost, travel, materials, cancellation terms and the expected collection date.

The teaching observation and customer requirements help identify preparation and delivery work that a classroom-revenue calculation would miss. No fictional profit or successful learning result is assumed. Multiplying a full classroom’s gross revenue by every working day is not evidence of likely profit.

sections.heading: Connect course economics with realistic delivery
paragraphs: Price preparation, customer acquisition and realistic utilisation alongside classroom time. Record which cancellations or customer approval conditions affect cash and what resources the brand must continue to supply. SBA’s finance guidance is a reference for the accounting and cash distinction, not a source of actual demand.

Keep outcome claims tied to actual evidence and the credential’s true status. If the course is changed or marketed for a different purpose, revisit the relevant rights and permission questions rather than reusing an old workshop description.

sections.heading: Prepare the course-and-delivery factsheet
paragraphs: Create a document showing the course, actual audience, promised credential, materials/translation rights, instructor approval, revision responsibility and remaining legal questions. That makes the product understandable to the partner and to the people who will teach it.
bullets: Describe attendance and qualification claims precisely.
Identify sector and education questions before promotion.
Record actual material rights and update ownership.
Observe another instructor against defined criteria.
Price preparation, utilisation and acquisition rather than only classroom sales.

practicalOutput: A course-and-delivery factsheet explaining the credential, content rights, instructor evidence, realistic costs and unresolved permission questions.
limitations: No professional or education authorisation determination.
